title: The administration home operation, its fields, its parameter name, its entitlement rule and its record code are not in the sources
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-006); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: No source names the entitlement read of the administration surface or its path, the fields of its answer, the parameter row that holds its cache lifetime, the rule that decides whether a capability area may be opened (and which areas are read-only), or the decision-record code of an open.
evidence: RWB-E8-006 gives one screen and two endpoints (POST /admin/reference-loads and POST /admin/rule-versions), both of which are other services' now; FSD P4 v3 A2.17 gives the intent, the metric, the validation rule VR-P4-017-1 and BR-P4-017 but no operation; TSD P4 v3 T-A lists API-P4-007 GET /admin/roles, API-P4-008 GET /admin/access-log and API-P4-012 GET /me/session and no entitlement or home operation; Architecture v5 slide 14 gives the P4 contract as authorise, me/permissions, doa-limits and masking-policies; DP-03 gives the local record library and its topic but not the code of a read.
proposed: Provide one read GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/home answering an AdminHome of one area row per capability area in force with capabilityArea, letters, scope and mayOpen, plus matrixVersion, maskingVersion, listVersion, roleClass, chain and recordedAt; hold the cache lifetime in the parameter row access.home.cache.ttl.seconds read through DP-06; use the library's read code for the open entry; leave the composite route and the panel lists to RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

title: The rule-change request record while the registry, the load gate and the approval belong to other stories
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-007); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
description: Five values of this key are not in the sources: the P7 rule-package contract dependency that the two registry reads need, since the metadata contract-dependency list of the key carries only RWB-P3-E1042-CON; the operation POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/rule-changes and the read beside it, with their fields; the field-level placement of a change inside an entry of the local decision-record chain and the field-level shape of dryRunCounts; the record code an administrative change is written under; and the statement of which version states the change request accepts and which it only observes.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T6.3 fixes the seven-item change checklist, its DF-REF-295 column and the message ID MSG-P3-022, and T4 fixes the version lifecycle LOADED, VALIDATED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK and REFUSED, but no operation of the P4 appendix T-A records a change request: API-P4-014 to API-P4-021 are the registry's own operations, and the ownership map puts them and the four rule tables with P7 (ASM-A6-api-3, ASM-A6-tables-3). The legacy story RWB-E8-007 names POST /admin/rule-versions and its approve, which are the load gate of RWB-P4-AD011-APP and the approval of RWB-P4-AD012-APP and are not this slice. The Temporal and Drools design slide 15 puts the whole governance of a version in rwb-decision and the change to data with no release, and names no administration record of the change outside the registry.
proposed: Build the change request as a record of rwb-access: one entry of the local decision-record chain of DP-03 that binds the registry version, its test evidence and the approving role RW-RISK, with the two registry reads declared as consumed against the P7 rule-package contract and its fake, the missing C dependency raised at D1 and not added to the metadata, the seven checklist item codes and the seven version states fixed as contract constants of TSD P4 v3 T6.3 and T4, and the approval and the 00:01 promotion left to the registry.

title: The limit-move writes, their fields, the state set and the reference-list check are not in the sources
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-008)
description: The two writes that move one delegation_limit row (PATCH /doa-limits/{delegationLimitId} and POST /doa-limits/{delegationLimitId}/approve), their request and answer fields, the limit_version scheme, the lifecycle state set of a moved row, the record code of a move and the text of MSG-P7-002 are not in the sources; and this story's pattern list carries no DP-07 and its contract-dependency list no RWB-P3-E1043-CON, so no reference-data list check for the decision codes, the levels and the product groups is available to it.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.19 names the journey and two rules (VR-P4-019-1, BR-P4-019) and no operation, no field and no state; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 lists the delegation_limit columns and T3.2 the lists LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-DECISION and LOV-PRODUCT, and T4 gives a lifecycle for a rule package version only; Architecture v5 slide 14 names GET /doa-limits and the DoaLimitChanged event and no write on the table; the Temporal and Drools design fixes the approve-and-date discipline and no state name; the legacy story RWB-E8-008 carries the two rule-version endpoints and no delegation endpoint.
proposed: Fix the two paths on /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits/{delegationLimitId} and the field set in RWB-P4-E8008-CON, fix the state set PENDING_APPROVAL, IN_FORCE and SUPERSEDED, take the decision code, the level and the product group of a moved row from the row it moves rather than from a list this service does not hold, and carry the message ID MSG-P7-002 with its text left to the message catalogue.

title: Treatment policy edition: the P3 reference-load contract is not a declared dependency, the table code, the workbook part names, the field detail and the record code are unspecified, and the four sources conflict on who holds the right
source: Legacy RWB-E8-009 in 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (story statement, permission checks, data table); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.20 (intent, description, VR-P4-020-1, BR-P4-020, roles, ACs); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.2, T4, T6.1 and appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P4-004 to API-P4-010); Program BRD REQ-S2-004 and REQ-DRI-010; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (lov_value, reference_version, reference_row, treatment, POST /admin/reference-loads, GET /admin/parameters); Template and Rules v1 section R3 R-PREC
description: Five values of this key are absent from the sources and one of them is a conflict. (1) The reference-load contract dependency: the story hands the workbook to P3 rwb-case POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads, and the contract-dependencies row of RWB-P4-E8009-APP carries only RWB-P3-E1042-CON, so no P3 reference-load or reference-data contract is declared; the call is built against that contract and its fake and the missing dependency is raised here rather than added to the metadata. (2) The table code the file is handed over with is not in any source; this story uses product_policy. (3) The three parts of the edition are named as the bands, the floors and the ranges in the story statement, but the sheet names, the header rows, the accepted media types, the upload size cap and the exact field detail of the request and of the answer are not written anywhere. (4) The record code that marks an edition entry in the local decision-record chain is not in any source. (5) The screen that carries the edition is not named: the legacy story names SCR-39 Rules and parameters and SCR-41 Delegation of authority and the edition sits on neither. (6) The conflict: the legacy permission table gives the C letter to RW-COE and the A letter to RW-RISK, FSD P4 v3 A2.20.3.3 makes the product head the primary role, and TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives RW-PRODHEAD R only in Rules and parameters. R-PREC puts the Technical Specifications above the story master, so the product head proposes and cannot submit, the C letter is RW-COE's and the A letter RW-RISK's; the story tests exactly that, with a product head holding R refused 403 with MSG-P4-002.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E8-009 gives the story sentence, two ACs, a permission table (Rules and parameters C: RW-COE; A: RW-RISK) and a data table naming treatment, decision_log_entry, rule_row and role, and no request shape; FSD P4 v3 A2.20 gives VR-P4-020-1, BR-P4-020, the primary role table and AC-P4-020-01 but no field of the edition and no operation; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 gives LOV-PRODUCT (MORTGAGE, HIRE_PURCHASE, SSME, UNSECURED) and LOV-VERSION-STATUS and T-A.1 and T-A.2 give API-P4-004 to API-P4-010 with no product-policy path, no load read and no product_policy table code, and T6.1 gives RW-PRODHEAD R only; ownership.json puts lov_value, reference_version and reference_row with P3 (ASM-A6-tables-5), the reference-load and list paths with P3 (ASM-A6-api-4) and treatment with S2; no source names the table code, the sheet names or the record code
proposed: Keep the two operations under the access base and hand the file unchanged to the P3 reference-load contract through its contract and fake, with the missing C dependency raised at D1; fix the table code, the sheet names, the upload cap and the record code with the owner and the ledger owner at contract review; keep the values with P3 and interpret none of them; read the rights as the technical specification has them, so the product head proposes with R and RW-COE holds the C letter that submits the edition, with the A letter a load approval on the console path

title: The rwb-comms template dependency, the two template operations, the approval fields and the approval-reference shape are not in the sources
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2.md; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (Ownership Map v1); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-010)
description: The template approval gate of rwb-access calls two rwb-comms operations, reads a version's state and author and records an approving role code, and none of these values is fixed by a source the story can use: the story's metadata carries no P6 contract dependency and the two P6 operations it consumes are not in its contract-dependency list; the read of one template by its id (GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates/{templateId}) is not in the P6 appendix, which declares the list with a code filter and not a read by id; the request and answer field set of the approval and of the history, the type of each field and the record code of an approval are not stated; the shape of the approval reference is not stated; the template table of TSD P6 v2 T3.1 carries no author and no lifecycle state of its own, so the author of a version is read from the standard record column created_by and the state from the standard record column state of T3.0; and this story's pattern list carries no DP-07 and its contract-dependency list no RWB-P3-E1043-CON, so the product group a version carries cannot be validated against LOV-PRODUCT here.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.21 names the journey, one validation rule (VR-P4-021-1) and one business rule (BR-P4-021) and no operation, no field and no state; TSD P4 v3 T6.3 states the author-and-approver rule with MSG-P7-002 and names no field of a template approval; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 lists the template, notice and merge_field columns with the standard record columns of T3.0, and appendix T-A the five P6 template operations API-P6-003 to API-P6-007, of which API-P6-004 uploads a version in state DRAFT and API-P6-006 takes a TemplateApproval request and answers a Template; the ownership map puts template, notice and merge_field in P6 (Architecture v5 slide 41) and lists GET /admin/templates, POST /admin/templates, GET /admin/templates/{templateId}/content and POST /admin/templates/{templateId}/approve, and no read of one template by id; Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access the two events AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged and no template event; the legacy story RWB-E8-010 names two rule-version endpoints and the rule-versions base of the monolith, and no template endpoint at all.
proposed: Build the approval and the history against the P6 template contract and its fake, publish that contract with the P6 contract story of the legacy key, and add the missing C dependency (RWB-P6-... or the id the P6 split allocates) to the metadata at D1; fix the two rwb-access paths on /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/template-approvals and the request and answer field set in RWB-P4-E8010-CON; hold the approval-reference shape as a parameter row; take the approving role as a role code from role and permission; read the author of a version from the standard record column created_by and the state from the standard record column state, and write no template state here; answer the history from the local decision-record chain; carry the message ID MSG-P7-002 with its text left to the message catalogue; and let the P6 owner confirm the read-by-id path or supply the code filter it prefers on the list operation.
